items.title: 56712_Cootie Williams oral history interview
items.q: I had taken Bubber Miley's place, and that was Bubber Miley's trademark, the plunger.

ctx.x: Well, listen. Just while we're talking about that, the plunger, one time when you and I were doing an interview earlier, you started talking to me about the plunger. Well, first of all, last time we talked you laughed about it and said that it seemed like funny to you. But afterwards, you told me that that just became a part of you.

Yeah, it did become a part of me, because that was what Duke Ellington hired me to do. And it dawned on me. I had taken Bubber Miley's place, and that was Bubber Miley's trademark, the plunger. And I was almost a legit trumpet player at that time. I had just left Fletcher Henderson's band, playing first trumpet. And coming in -- and I never used a plunger. Then by, you know, sitting and listening to Joe Tricky Sam Nanton, that's how I picked it up.
Well, but the thing is this, you know. You were pointing out that you had like two ways of being yourself. You -- I mean, as you said, Louis was your idol. And so you used to blow open horn.
